name: Monday Dev
description: Monday Dev is monday.com's product-development platform for planning roadmaps, managing sprints, prioritizing features, tracking bugs and incidents, coordinating releases, and monitoring engineering performance. It connects product, engineering, design, data, and customer-facing teams through linked boards, Agile views, automations, documents, dashboards, and development-tool integrations.
agentUseSummary: Do not create a separate Monday Dev connection or install. Connect the canonical Monday.com provider once, then use its bounded board, item, and update tools for explicitly selected dev boards under the existing Safe or Dangerously skip permissions policy. Relay does not expose semantic sprint, backlog, epic, roadmap, release, bug, incident, capacity, engineering-metric, CI/CD, automation, or dev-administration actions through this alias.

blocked.label: Create a separate monday dev connection
blocked.description: Monday dev uses the same monday user, account, OAuth grant, scopes, workspaces, boards, items, and updates as the canonical Monday.com provider; a second connection would duplicate identity and authority.

blocked.label: Install duplicate monday dev tools
blocked.description: Relay mounts supported monday board, item, and update operations once through the canonical Monday.com provider rather than publishing parallel dev tools, policies, and audit state.

blocked.label: Run separate monday dev actions
blocked.description: Supported bounded operations on explicitly selected dev boards belong to the canonical Monday.com connection and its existing Safe or Dangerously skip permissions profile.

blocked.label: Operate specialized development workflows
blocked.description: Semantic sprint, backlog, task, epic, feature, request, roadmap, release, bug, incident, retrospective, dependency, hierarchy, story-point, and capacity actions are outside Relay's current generic typed monday board and item contract.

blocked.label: Operate integrations or engineering intelligence
blocked.description: GitHub, GitLab, CircleCI, CI/CD, repository synchronization, Agile insights, velocity and burndown charts, engineering dashboards, AI summaries, documents, automations, notifications, imports, and exports are blocked.

blocked.label: Administer monday dev or use raw interfaces
blocked.description: Workspace, solution-folder, board, schema, user, team, permission, plan, billing, app, integration, and dev administration, destructive or bulk changes, webhooks, raw GraphQL, platform MCP, browser sessions, scraping, and private endpoints are blocked.

approvalProfiles.label: Use Monday.com
approvalProfiles.description: No separate monday dev action is enabled because the product shares the canonical Monday.com provider and only its bounded board, item, and update boundary is currently supported.

runtimeSupport.description: No duplicate monday dev tools are mounted. OpenClaw uses the canonical Monday.com provider for approved bounded operations on explicit dev boards and items.
No duplicate monday dev tools are mounted. Hermes uses the canonical Monday.com provider for approved bounded operations on explicit dev boards and items.

providerSetup.blocker: Monday dev is a specialized product on the shared monday platform, not a separate provider identity or authorization surface. Monday documents that its platform GraphQL API supports dev and that monday dev tasks and bugs are items in connected boards, while the same app OAuth grant controls account, workspace, board, and update access. Relay's canonical Monday.com provider already owns that OAuth lifecycle, account binding, typed connector, policies, runtime mounts, audit, and bounded board and item behavior. It does not implement the connected sprint, epic, capacity, roadmap, release, engineering-metric, repository-integration, or automation semantics that distinguish monday dev, so a duplicate card would both repeat authority and overstate support.
providerSetup.nextAction: Keep this product-mode slug non-installable and direct setup, connection, installation, and supported execution to the canonical Monday.com provider. Use only its explicit bounded board listing, board-item listing, item read, update read, local draft, approval-governed item create or update, and update-posting actions on customer-selected dev boards. Extend the canonical provider only after Relay separately specifies, implements, and accepts typed development resources and relationships with exact scopes, account and workspace binding, sprint and hierarchy invariants, repository authority, bounds, approvals, idempotency, audit, redaction, provider limits, and production verification.

evidence.supports: Monday describes monday dev as its product for roadmaps, sprints, feature requests, bug and incident tracking, releases, retrospectives, engineering metrics, documents, automations, and development-tool integrations.

Monday states that the shared GraphQL platform API supports monday dev along with work management, sales CRM, and service and operates on account resources including workspaces, boards, items, and column values.
Monday documents one app OAuth authorization against a selected monday account with granular account, workspace, board, and update scopes rather than separate monday dev credentials.
Monday documents dev tasks as items and sprints as groups and connected records across Tasks, Sprints, Epics, and hidden Capacity boards whose relationship invariants power the product.
Monday identifies dev-only GitHub and CircleCI integrations, roadmaps, epic insights, sprint automations, Agile insights, WIP limits, item cards, and engineering-performance dashboards.
Monday documents bugs as items in a Bugs Queue board combined with columns, automations, forms, dashboards, and widgets rather than a separate provider identity.
